To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the upper stratum or the half upper strata of elephant swards have the highest leaf proportion and C18:2 and C18:1 contents; 2) the lower strata of elephant have higher proportions of C16:0; 3) the half lower strata have the highest proportions of C18 and C18:0; 4) the upper strata have the lowest proportion of C18 and 18:0 and the highest proportion of C18
the proportion of C18-3 in elephant grass sward was higher in the 90 cm sward and in the half-upper stratum.
the proportion of C18 fatty acids (C18:1, C18:2, C18:3), which are precursors to CLA, were higher in the upper stratum and in the swards with 90-cm pre-grazing height.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fatty acid composition in the vertical stratum of elephant grass swards and the effects of pre-grazing height (90 or 100 cm) and levels of removal of pre-grazing (50% or70%).
the morphological and chemical composition of elephant grass sward subjected to grazing heights and level of defoliations.

the morphological and chemical characteristics of the vertical strata in elephant grass sward and the potential to use the vertical strata to manage the fatty acid composition of meat and milk from grazing animals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a grazing height of 90 cm, a grazing management that results in a higher leaf proportion, and a higher proportion of C3 grasses in the sward, would be the best way to increase the proportion of C18 in the diet of ruminants grazing in tropical pastures.
the fatty acid profile in elephant grass sward is dependent on the level of defoliations and pre-grazing heights.
the fatty acid profile of elephant grass can be modified through grazing management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the upper stratum (or the first-last stocking) of elephant grass provides the animals grazing in this sward with a higher proportion of C 18:3 and higher crude protein content.

grazing management schemes (e.g. 50% removal of the 90 cm pre-grazing height) and grazing strata that result in a higher proportion and quality of leaf blades (higher C18:3) should be used to improve the fatty acid profile of milk and meat from dairy cattle grazing in elephant grass pastures.
a grazing height of 90 cm with 50% defoliation and the upper stratum would provide the highest C18:3 proportions to animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
grazing management schemes can be used to modify the proportion of C18-3 in the diet of grazing animals.
the fatty acid profiles of the elephant grass sward are influenced by the level of defolation, grazing height and grazing stratum.
grazing management schemes can be used to manipulate the fatty acid composition of the grass swards, and therefore, to manipulate the fatty acids profile of the milk or meat of grazing animals.
